subject: [Exec update] Private upgrades: timeline, rollback policy (v1), and GA gates
body:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:18 AM
Subject: [Exec update] Private upgrades: timeline, rollback policy (v1), and GA gates

All,

Sharing an exec-level update for the “Private upgrade + rollback mechanism” workstream. This is the first time we’ll have a repeatable, supportable upgrade workflow for Private (VPC + on-prem), with explicit rollback hooks and guardrails.

Links (most relevant):
- PRD: PM-482 (Linear)
- Initiative tracker: ENG-2314 (Linear)
- Rollback/downgrade policy (current draft): Confluence “rollback-policy-and-downgrade-compatibility”
- Runbook draft (SRE/operator): Confluence “private-upgrade-runbook”

Timeline (still tracking to the original 4-phase plan):
1) Phase 1 (requirements + design): complete this week (design doc + ADRs mostly done)
2) Phase 2 (implementation): target 4–6 weeks
   - prechecks framework + compatibility enforcement
   - backup primitives (DB + config state) + verification
   - orchestration (staged apply + health gates) and rollback hooks
   - structured telemetry + diagnostics bundle output
3) Phase 3 (hardening + beta): 2–3 weeks
   - failure injection matrix (disk full, image pull fail, schema mismatch, API unavailable)
   - beta with 1–2 customers (Markus’ team leading)
4) Phase 4 (GA readiness): 1–2 weeks
   - support enablement + required dashboards/alerts + runbook final

Key risks / decision points
1) Downgrade semantics vs. data migrations (largest risk)
   - v1 stance we’re proposing: rollback is supported only when migrations are reversible OR explicitly marked rollback-safe.
   - forward-only DB migrations will block rollback past that boundary (installer will refuse + instruct operator).
   - we will not claim “arbitrary downgrade to any prior version” for v1.

2) Air-gapped artifact integrity (mandatory)
   - offline bundle import must verify signatures; any verification failure is a hard stop.
   - Security’s requirements on key custody + rotation will affect GA gating.

3) Upgrade safety (partial upgrades)
   - we’re adding deterministic ordering + health gates, but we need to be honest that some environments will still experience downtime depending on customer topology and maintenance window.

GA gates (proposed)
- Pass upgrade simulation matrix in CI + at least one end-to-end rehearsal in staging with failure injection.
- Beta: 2 successful customer upgrades (1x VPC, 1x on-prem preferred) with runbook + Support involvement.
- Required telemetry: step timing metrics, failure counts, rollback triggers, correlation id propagation, and diagnostics tarball.
- Runbook completeness + Support escalation checklist.

What rollback WILL support in v1 (proposed)
- Rollback of chart/app versions to previous known good when:
  - prechecks pass
  - backups exist and verify
  - no forward-only migration has been executed (or rollback is explicitly supported)
- Automated rollback trigger on certain failure classes (e.g., backup verification failure, post-upgrade smoke test failure) with clear operator prompts.

What rollback will NOT support in v1
- “Downgrade across major versions” when DB schema is forward-only.
- Rollback after operator has continued past an explicitly flagged “rollback-unsafe boundary.”
- Guaranteed zero downtime across all customer environments.

Asks from you
1) Alignment on the v1 downgrade/rollback stance above (esp. the hard block on rollback past forward-only migrations).
2) Confirm GA gating requirements are sufficient (or if we need additional exec-level gates).

Attaching:
- GA checklist v0.7 (working copy)
- Runbook draft PDF (for quick skim; canonical version is in Confluence)

Thanks,
Vivek

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Product, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference



From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:02 AM
Subject: Re: [Exec update] Private upgrades: timeline, rollback policy (v1), and GA gates

Thanks Vivek.

I’m aligned with “installer refuses” rollback past forward-only boundaries. Please make sure:
- the boundary is provable (metadata table / explicit markers), not “best guess”
- refusal comes with a crisp operator message + support playbook

For air-gapped: signature verification must be hard-fail and should emit an audit log event (“bundle verification failed”) without leaking sensitive paths/keys.

Marcus — can you confirm we’re comfortable with the proposed key custody + rotation steps as GA gate? If not, call out now.

Aisha



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 12:26 PM
Subject: Re: [Exec update] Private upgrades: timeline, rollback policy (v1), and GA gates

+1 on the rollback stance.

From SRE side, I’d like one more explicit GA gate:
- “Rollback drill” in staging: deliberately fail an upgrade mid-way and validate we can restore service health within a target window.

We can pick a target that’s realistic (e.g., <60 min end-to-end including restore) and treat it as “must not regress” rather than a universal SLA.

Also: backup duration is going to be a recurring customer complaint. We should make sure runbook includes how to estimate backup time before starting the maintenance window.

Sean



From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 9:07 AM
Subject: Re: [Exec update] Private upgrades: timeline, rollback policy (v1), and GA gates

Confirming Security position for GA:

Required (GA gate):
1) Signed offline bundles, installer verification hard-fail.
2) Provenance metadata in the manifest (at minimum: build id, version, sha256 list).
3) Audit log events for upgrade/rollback actions + bundle verification failure.

Strongly recommended (can be post-GA if needed, but prefer in GA):
4) Documented key rotation process (who/when/how) and how customers get updated public keys in air-gapped.

Connor + Hanae are working through the practical bits with Release Eng. I’ll follow up with a short “acceptable GA” checklist we can lock.

Marcus



From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 4:41 PM
Subject: Re: [Exec update] Private upgrades: timeline, rollback policy (v1), and GA gates

Got it — I’m adding the explicit rollback drill gate (staging failure injection + time-to-restore target) into the GA checklist.

On “provable boundary”: Ethan/Michael have the migration metadata table work underway so the installer can make a deterministic decision (and show the exact migration id that blocks rollback). We’ll also include the operator-facing message + support playbook section.

Action items I’m taking:
- Update GA checklist (v0.8) to include:
  - rollback drill gate
  - security GA gates (1–3 required, 4 flagged as “preferred by GA / required by first on-prem GA customer”)
- Update PRD language to be unambiguous: “Rollback within the supported window; downgrade past forward-only migrations is not supported.”

Dev — once I update the PRD + Confluence policy page, can you sanity check the customer-facing phrasing for Support?

Vivek



From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 20, 2025 at 4:42 PM
Subject: Re: [Exec update] Private upgrades: timeline, rollback policy (v1), and GA gates

Yes — happy to review.

Request: in the operator UX, please ensure the refusal to rollback isn’t framed as “unexpected error.” It needs to clearly say:
- rollback blocked due to migration X marked forward-only
- next best action (restore from backup to the same version / contact Support / open ticket)
- where to find diagnostics bundle

If we can keep the “what to do next” to 2–3 bullets, Support will thank you.

Dev

—
Dev Patel
Support Enablement Lead
Redwood Inference
